How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (5)

  1. In what year was Trend Micro founded, and under what legal entity?
    The founding date anchors the vendor's operating history.
  2. Has Trend Micro made any workforce reductions in the last 24 months, and which functions were affected?
    Workforce reductions can affect support and product delivery.
  3. Has Trend Micro lost any large enterprise or financial-services customers in the last 24 months, and why?
    Loss of large customers can signal product or service problems.
  4. Have there been any unplanned executive departures, misconduct findings or governance disputes at Trend Micro in the last 24 months?
    Leadership instability or misconduct can affect vendor direction and reputation.
  5. What are Trend Micro's list prices and licensing metrics for TrendAI Vision One Endpoint Security and its managed service options?
    Public pricing lets a bank benchmark quotes.

Timeline

  1. 2026-07-20 · litigation Trend Micro
    Federal dockets show two suits filed against Trend Micro in W.D. Tex. in 2025-2026

    According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): ZapFraud Inc. v. Trend Micro Incorporated, a patent suit, was filed on 2026-07-20, and Congruent Media Resourcing LLC v. Trend Micro Incorporated was filed on 2025-11-13, both in the Western District of Texas. Neither shows a termination date. The claims were not reviewed. Free Law Project (CourtListener) (primary filing, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-03-23 · rebrand Trend Micro
    Trend Micro renames its enterprise business TrendAI

    Trend Micro announced that its enterprise cybersecurity business now operates under the name TrendAI, with the platform named TrendAI Vision One. The listed company remains Trend Micro Incorporated; the release names Rachel Jin as head of TrendAI. Trend Micro (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  3. 2025-08-05 · security incident Trend Micro
    Trend Micro warns of exploited command injection flaws in on-premises Apex One

    Reported by SecurityWeek and Help Net Security on 2025-08-06: Trend Micro disclosed two command injection vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-54948 and CVE-2025-54987) in the management console of on-premises Apex One, said it had seen at least one attempt to exploit one of them, and issued a temporary fix tool ahead of a patch expected in mid-August 2025. The affected product is the on-premises predecessor line, not the product tracked here.
